ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 19, 22 through 34, 289, 292, 297, 302, 314, and 330; Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10606, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; Financial Services Commission customer due diligence and transaction reporting rules; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 9161, as amended) and Enforcement Decree foreign investment reporting provisions; Real Name Financial Transaction and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5493, as amended). No public beneficial ownership register exists; UBO data is maintained by financial institutions and is accessible to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and other authorized government authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation Registration (Certificate of Registered Corporate Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office / Supreme Court Internet Registration Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the destination state is a Hague Apostille Convention member: notarize before a Korean notary public if required, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If the destination state is not an Apostille member: notarize if required, obtain a certificate of authentication from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, and then submit to the Embassy/Consulate of the destination country for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative and mutually exclusive paths; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Registration Extract / Subsistence Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the Local District Court of Korea / Supreme Court Internet Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: registry extract plus, if required, notarization, followed by an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular path: registry extract, notarization if required, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication certificate followed by legalization at the destination country's Embassy/Consulate in Korea. Use only one path depending on the destination state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney Authorizing Incorporation and Bank Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa / corporate secretary / incoming directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: execute and notarize the resolution or power of attorney before a Korean notary public, then attach an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-Apostille states: execute and notarize, obtain the Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication certificate, then submit to the destination state's Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization. No sequential combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and District Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague member state: notarize the certified copy or use the court-issued certified extract, then obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Non-Hague member state: notarize and obtain the Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication certificate, then apply for consular legalization at the destination state's Embassy/Consulate in Korea. Choose the path that is legally required by the destination state; the two methods are exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Corporate Bank for the FBA Seller Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank maintaining the corporate operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue the letter on bank letterhead with the branch manager's signature and corporate seal impression, then the document is notarized before a Korean notary public. If the destination is an Apostille state, issue an Apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If the destination is not an Apostille state, obtain the Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication certificate and then consular legalization by the destination country's Embassy/Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and never used in sequence.

stage_1.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct and ultimate beneficial owners, shareholders above the 25% threshold, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and agents of the Chikushoesa must be screened continuously against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's designated terrorist assets list, Korean Financial Services Commission enforcement and sanctions databases, and domestic court/regulator proceedings. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for overseas politically exposed persons, domestic senior public officials, their family members, and close associates. For each PEP, senior management approval, documentation of source of wealth and source of funds, ongoing transaction monitoring, and adverse media screening must be completed before incorporation. Any potential match or negative hit triggers immediate escalation, a Suspicious Transaction Report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, and a hold on all formation steps until the hit is positively cleared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) / Local District Court Registry Office Trade Name Reservation System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and the Registration of Real Estate and Other Property regulations, a corporate trade name must be registered in Hangul and the corporate form suffix must indicate 'Chusik Hoesa' for a stock company. Foreign or Romanized names may be presented in parentheses only as transliterations; the registered Hangul name is the controlling name for uniqueness, priority, and enforcement. Name clearance follows a four-tier framework: (1) the natural use word or brand, including any foreign trademark; (2) the Korean Hangul transliteration or equivalent; (3) the corporate form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' or 'Stock Company'; and (4) a distinguishing descriptor when the identical name already exists. Misleading, scandalous, or likely-confusing names are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry officer rejects a trade name reservation, the applicant may file a written objection or immediate appeal under the Korean Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act with the district court having jurisdiction over the registry office, generally within two weeks of the rejection notice. The appeal must attach the rejection notice, proof of payment, the proposed name, and a legal memorandum demonstrating the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name and does not contain a prohibited or sensitive token. If the court dismisses the appeal, the applicant may pursue a further appeal to the Supreme Court on questions of law only, or submit a fresh reservation with a modified and distinct Hangul name. A name reservation may be extended by filing a timely renewal before expiry, subject to the availability of the name at that time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or mail-forwarding service is generally rejected by Korean tax authorities and banks for an internet retail and Amazon FBA entity. The National Tax Service requires an actual place of business with a valid commercial lease or serviced office agreement for corporate income tax and VAT registration, and a mail-only address will not support the issuance of a valid business registration certificate. Banks applying the Real Name Financial Transaction and Confidentiality Act and AML customer due diligence standards require the registered head office to be physically visitable, with a signboard or nameplate, power and internet services in the corporate name, and a responsible person reasonably available. A dedicated desk or serviced suite in a licensed co-working or business incubator may be accepted only if a formal lease and landlord certificate are provided; a pure virtual office without a physical office presence is not permissible for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist used by authorities and banks: (1) lease contract for the head office; (2) corporate nameplate or signage; (3) utility, internet, and phone bills in the corporate name; (4) availability of a director or authorized representative; (5) presence of administrative records or a work station; (6) evidence that the operation is not solely conducted from an overseas FBA warehouse. Quantified risk: approximately 25-40% for a first-year entity using a shared or serviced office, and above 70% for a pure virtual address or P.O. Box; the Korean National Tax Service may conduct tax address surveys and local banks routinely schedule on-site compliance visits before and after account opening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 5057, as amended; specifically Articles 288 through 300, Article 317, Article 363, and Article 393, together with the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Company Registration Division, Registration Office, the District Court having jurisdiction over the company registered office; post-registration business registration is completed at the local Business Registration Office of the National Tax Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Charter) together with the Application for Corporation Registration in the Republic of Korea, filed through the official court registration system and the I-REO company registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act; however, all subscribed shares must be fully paid into a designated capital deposit escrow account maintained by a licensed commercial bank or securities company before incorporation registration under Article 295. The deposited funds are blocked from withdrawal until the company receives its certificate of incorporation registration. A paid-in capital of at least KRW 10,000,000 is practically recommended for corporate bank account opening, Amazon seller verification, and cross-border payment processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Approval, and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Korea and the company online registration system I-REO operated under the Supreme Court registration authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must convene a promoters meeting and adopt the draft Articles of Incorporation. The articles must state the corporate objective covering ISIC 4791 internet retail sale, marketplace fulfillment, cross-border e-commerce, and general trade. Every promoter must sign and seal the final articles, and the document must be notarized by a notary public licensed in Korea. Before notarization, we perform a name availability search through the I-REO court registration system and confirm that no identical name is registered. The notarized articles serve as the constitutional instrument for the subsequent incorporation application and must contain the company name, Chusik Hoesa designation, registered address, capital, share classes, directors, auditors, and corporate governance rules.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Corporate name availability search result
Promoter identification documents or passports
Power of attorney if a promoter is represented
Notarization fee receipt and notarized charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or court registration system identifies an invalid clause or a corporate name conflict, the promoters must amend the articles, adopt a new name, re-notarize the corrected version, and resubmit without additional court adjudication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Subscription and Payment into Blocked Capital Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank or securities company in the Republic of Korea acting as the capital depository under Article 295 of the Commercial Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the promoters must subscribe all shares. Each subscriber executes a subscription statement and pays the full amount of the subscription price into a capital deposit account opened in the name of the proposed company at a commercial bank or securities company in Korea. The financial institution must certify the deposit and agree that the funds cannot be withdrawn until the court has completed the incorporation registration. If any subscriber contributes property, an independent appraiser must issue an appraisal report and the board must include the valuation in the deposit certificate process. The exact paid-in amount must satisfy the amount stated in the Articles; no statutory minimum is imposed by law, but at least KRW 10,000,000 is recommended for practical banking and vendor procedures.
required_dossiers: Share subscription statement for every promoter
Capital deposit certificate from the financial institution
Certified copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or corporate identification of subscribers
In-kind property appraisal report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit certificate is incomplete or the subscriber has failed to pay the full amount, the bank must issue a corrected certificate after the deficiency is cured or the subscription must be re-opened and repurchased.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court and Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, followed by the Business Registration Office of the competent local tax office under the National Tax Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative or authorized representative submits the incorporation registration application to the Registration Division of the District Court within two weeks of the payment deposit. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles, a certificate of capital payment, proof of officers appointment and consent, and the registered seal specimen. The court reviews the application under the Commercial Act and, if satisfied, issues the corporation registration certificate. After the registration, the company must file a business registration application with the National Tax Service office having jurisdiction over the registered office within 14 days to obtain the Business Registration Certificate and commence taxable operations.
required_dossiers: Application for Corporation Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Consent and appointment statements of directors and auditor
Certificate of subscribed capital and dividend evidence
Corporate seal specimen
Lease agreement or ownership proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues an order to supplement or correct, the applicant has two weeks to file the missing documents; if the business registration is queried, the company must submit corrected address proof and a revised business income code and re-file without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Statutory Officer Appointment, Corporate Seal Registration, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, the District Court for corporate seal certification, the commercial bank for corporate accounts, and KOTRA or the receiving domestic bank for foreign investment declaration if non-resident shareholders are involved.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The newly registered corporation must hold its first board meeting and pass the formal first board resolution, which ratifies the subscription, designates the registered office, appoints the representative director and statutory officers, adopts the corporate seal, and approves bank account opening. The directors and officers must present identity documents, and the corporate seal certificate must be obtained from the district court registry. The company must then open a Korean Won and foreign currency account at the chosen bank. If the company is foreign-invested, file the foreign investment declaration through KOTRA or the receiving domestic bank before issuing shares; this step is time-sensitive and must be completed before any foreign payment is made into the corporate account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporation registration
Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal certificate
Minutes of the first board meeting
Notarized corporate resolution
Passports or ID cards of directors and officers
Bank account application and signatory forms
Foreign investment report and supporting affidavit, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional anti-money laundering verification, the authorized representatives must submit source-of-funds documents and a board resolution explaining the corporate treasury structure; if the foreign investment report is rejected, the submission must be reclassified and re-filed at KOTRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: E-Commerce Seller Compliance, Mail-Order Seller Registration, and Amazon FBA Seller Account Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Si-Gun-Gu Community Office or E-Commerce Supervisory Authority under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce; Amazon Seller Central for merchant identity verification; National Tax Service for e-commerce tax administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must complete e-commerce seller compliance by registering as a mail-order seller with the competent local government office. The registration certificate must identify the corporate business registration number and the internet retail sales business code. The company must then complete Amazon Professional Seller account verification using the Business Registration Certificate, corporate bank account, and corporate officer identification. For cross-border sales, the tax agent shall advise on whether transactions are treated as Korean-source export sales or taxable domestic supplies under the Value Added Tax Act. This operational step ensures that Amazon FBA receipts can be reported lawfully and that the company has the necessary corporate identity documentation for platform and payment gateway approval.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Mail-order seller registration application
Amazon seller account identity verification documents
Corporate seal certificate and officer passports
Bank account statement or proof of bank account
Power of attorney for tax agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the mail-order seller registration is refused, correct the business address and representative details and refile with the local government; if Amazon rejects seller verification, resubmit updated notarized documents and a certified English translation of the Business Registration Certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is engaged in ISIC 4791 internet-based retail sales through marketplace FBA fulfillment and does not own or operate a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility in Korea.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is required for this pure online retail and marketplace business model; the company only needs ordinary corporate registration, business tax registration, and mail-order seller notification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea has no jurisdiction over an online sales operation without physical production or hazardous processes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no Environmental Impact Assessment registration or environmental approval is triggered because the company will not operate manufacturing facilities, chemical plants, or industrial storage installations subject to the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company does not generate wastewater, volatile organic compounds, hazardous emissions, or industrial waste; any office or warehouse used by Amazon fulfillment centers is outside the entity operational scope and regulated by the third-party facility operator.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required for the formation stage of an online marketplace seller. If the company later establishes its own distribution or storage facility, the operator must obtain a building fire safety certificate from the local fire station, a workplace safety registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and, for any storage space exceeding statutory thresholds, a hazardous substance handling or logistics center permit before operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), Government Complex-Sejong; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); customs clearance counterpart: Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must apply for a Business Registration Certificate from the competent Korean District Tax Office or online through HomeTax by filing a business registration application. Required attachments include: the foreign corporation's certificate of incorporation, articles of association, evidence of a registered Korean place of business or fixed establishment (including an Amazon FBA dedicated point of presence), identity documentation of the legal representative and/or resident tax agent with power of attorney, and a completed non-resident taxpayer registration form. Upon approval the NTS assigns a 10-digit registered business number which serves simultaneously as the Korean Tax Identification Number and VAT Identification Number. The entity must then subscribe to the HomeTax electronic tax invoice (e-invoice) system, open a bank account at a Korean licensed bank for export proceeds, and notify NTS of any changes to business data within 15 days. A Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation for tax purposes and must register regardless of revenue level or foreign ownership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election mechanisms; a Chusik Hoesa is unconditionally taxed at entity level under the Korean Corporate Tax Act and is not eligible for pass-through treatment or a unilateral hybrid election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis VAT registration threshold for corporations; a Chusik Hoesa must register before commencing business. Small individual merchants with annual turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000 may use simplified taxable status, but this threshold exemption does not apply to companies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued as electronic tax invoices (e-invoices) and transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system within one day after the taxable supply. Businesses must integrate batch transmission via NTS-approved EDI/API channels; there is no private physical fiscal stamp, but anti-fraud is enforced through mandatory digital certificates, timestamp circulation, automatic e-invoice matching, and cross-validation of export declarations with Korea Customs Service records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to goods physically exported from Korea to a foreign market, including cross-border e-commerce dispatches from Korean FBA warehouses, provided the export has a valid export declaration and the supplier receives export proceeds from a foreign buyer. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated where the place of supply is outside Korea and consumption occurs offshore. Sales delivered and consumed inside Korea via Amazon Korea or domestic channels are standard-rated at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic Export Declaration (Bill of Export / separate export clearance equivalent to a Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading (ocean or air) or combined transport house waybill proving the goods left Korea
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation from a Korean licensed bank evidencing foreign currency repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the 0% rate is claimed but the required customs, logistics, invoice, or foreign-exchange evidence is missing or inconsistent, the NTS reclassifies the supply as domestic at 10% VAT and imposes statutory additional taxes, including unintentional underreporting penalties of 10% of the tax payable, negligent non-filing penalties of 20%, intentional fraud penalties of 40%, plus value-added surtax interest. Issuing or procuring a false export declaration or false e-invoice additionally triggers criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Korea Customs Act, carrying imprisonment not exceeding three years and fines up to five times the evaded amount, with retrospective clawback of all zero-rated input VAT previously credited or refunded and potential suspension of export VAT refund eligibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting through the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) and delegated foreign exchange banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but carefully supervised foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions such as trade settlements, direct operating expenses, and profit remittances, subject only to documentary verification and reporting to a foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, equity injections, and cross-border loans, are not freely convertible without prior or simultaneous reporting and registration. There is no mandatory surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in foreign exchange accounts with authorised domestic banks. Profit remittances by a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa are permitted once the statutory taxpayer or dividends have been properly documented, but they require filing of a foreign exchange receipt/payment report with the settlement bank and evidence of underlying earnings, tax clearance, and audited financial statements to ensure no undisclosed obligations exist. For Amazon FBA e-commerce operations, typical inflows are USD or EUR received via Amazon Pay and other PSPs, which must be routed through a domestic bank without violating the requirement that all cross-border claims be settled in Korea. The practical hurdle is not convertibility of the won for legitimate trade and investment, but the need for accurate purpose codes, underlying trade documentation, and a transparent corporate treasury trail that satisfies the bank's anti-money laundering and foreign exchange monitoring obligations. In practice, the BOK and MOEF can request flow-of-funds explanations, and any significant deviation between declared e-commerce turnover and bank receipts will trigger enhanced due diligence or sanctions. Overall, the won is convertible for genuine business and investment flows, but every transfer must be traceable and supported by a complete documentation suite.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Enforcement Decree of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds for e-commerce sales such as Amazon FBA must be collected and brought into Korea within 18 months from the export declaration date. There is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio: 0% of export proceeds must be converted into Korean won, and 100% may remain in a foreign currency account at an authorised foreign exchange bank. The exporter must submit a foreign exchange receipt report to the bank within the settlement period. If collection cannot be completed within the 18-month deadline, an extension must be requested from the relevant foreign exchange bank or MOEF before the deadline expires. For Amazon FBA settlements, the net proceeds from Amazon Pay are normally received by the Korean seller as marketplace remittances; these are classified as export proceeds and must be credited to the corporate foreign currency account and reported as such, with Seller Central statements, customs declarations, and VAT evidence retained for audit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Direct fintech EMI onboarding for a Korean-domiciled Chusik Hoesa is legally restricted. Airwallex, Stripe, and similar cross-border digital payment providers are not licensed as banks in South Korea and cannot open domestic KRW settlement accounts unless they are registered as electronic financial business operators under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act of the Financial Services Commission. As a practical matter, these EMIs must partner with a domestic licensed bank to provide settlement rails, which introduces layered KYC and may conflict with the bank's requirement that the entity maintain primary operating relationships with the local branch. The viability rating is Low-to-Medium: Airwallex and Stripe can support pay-in and pay-out via partner banks, but the statutory foreign exchange reporting and capital verification obligations still require a domestic banking relationship. The critical legal constraint is that any foreign EMI that processes KRW payments without a domestic banking partner would be operating unlawfully, and Korean banks will refuse to accept settlement from unlicensed overseas PSPs. The safest approach is to use a domestic tier-1 bank as the settlement node, with Amazon Pay and Stripe acting only as collection funnels for foreign currency, never as the primary KRW treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance by statutory directors is generally mandatory for opening a corporate KRW operating account. Foreign directors of the Chusik Hoesa cannot open a fully functional account solely through a remote consular proxy unless the Korean bank specifically allows a notarised power of attorney, the director's passport is apostilled or consul-legalised, and the bank's compliance officer conducts a live video interview. For a capital escrow account, the foreign shareholder or an authorised officer must usually appear in the bank branch to present the company seal, board resolution, and original certificate of incorporation. Remote opening is practically unavailable to first-time foreign corporate clients; in unusual cases where a foreign director is abroad, the bank may accept a consular-notarised POA plus a video interview, but this is discretionary and not a statutory right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The fund beneficiary is a non-resident foreign shareholder of a Korean Chusik Hoesa with no local corporate track record, creating a high-risk beneficial ownership profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and apostilled proof of identity for every shareholder and director, a certified registry extract showing the ownership chain, a bank reference letter from the shareholder's home-country bank with at least one year of transactional history, OSINT negative-media screening results, and a signed declaration of source of wealth and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The capital injection to be escrowed in South Korea is expected from an overseas corporate account belonging to the Amazon FBA parent or a third-party trading entity, which may mask money laundering through phantom trade transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised board resolution authorising the investment, a share subscription agreement and share allotment report, the original SWIFT MT103/202 remittance instruction with exact investor name and reference, a complete bank statement of the remitting company showing the source of funds, and a business plan explaining the commercial need for the capital in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity's principal payment rails are Amazon Pay, Stripe, and Airwallex, which may cause the Korean bank to reject settlement flows as unverified third-party payments or trade-based laundering channels.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed contract with Amazon Seller Central and each PSP, a periodic payout report from Amazon FBA showing itemised sales deductions and settlement amounts, matching customs export declarations (Kenote) for the e-commerce shipments, signed commercial invoices, shipping and logistics documents, and a flowchart from the compliance team explaining the exact flow of funds from the final consumer to the Korean corporate account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company may fail the Korean bank's documentary completeness test because its financial statements are prepared in a foreign currency and have no local auditor sign-off, casting doubt on its solvency and tax standing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign-currency financial statements translated into Korean and authorised by a certified public accountant, a local tax clearance certificate from the Korean National Tax Service, the enterprise registration certificate, VAT returns for prior e-commerce sales, and where applicable, an audited balance sheet from the parent company's home jurisdiction with apostille certification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be remitted in foreign currency (typically USD) to the Korea-based capital escrow account of the Chusik Hoesa at a tier-1 foreign exchange bank. The remittance instruction must include the purpose code for foreign direct investment or paid-in capital. The foreign shareholder must first file an FDI report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with KOTRA or the bank, obtain an FDI registration number, and ensure the remitter name on the SWIFT MT103 exactly matches the investor of record. After the bank receives funds, it will issue a Certificate of Foreign Exchange Receipt, which the company uses for capital verification at the registry and for subsequent tax filings. The bank will automatically report the inward remittance to BOK/FEIN; the company must not split the remittance to avoid reporting thresholds. For operational injection that exceeds the registered paid-in capital, the company must treat it as loan or capital increase and follow the applicable reporting rules under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. All Amazon FBA sale proceeds received from overseas marketplaces must also be credited to the designated foreign exchange account and reported, with supporting marketplace payout reports maintained for at least five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for Amazon FBA inventory, shipping, and logistics are cleared via SWIFT MT103 messages through the domestic foreign exchange bank, with each payment carrying the correct trade settlement purpose code and underlying documents including customs declarations, commercial invoices, and purchase orders. For larger procurement commitments, commercial LCs (letters of credit) and documentary collections are permissible where the Korean bank confirms the LC, with the bank relying on the shipping documents and bill of lading to release funds. KRW cannot be realistically used for inbound or outbound cross-border balances; all international treasury movements must be conducted in USD, EUR, or other acceptable settleable currencies. Amazon FBA disbursements into the Korean bank account may use Amazon's global payout system, but the bank must be able to identify the settlement source from a single named account, and the company must provide Amazon's periodic settlement reports converted into the required reporting format when asked by the bank.

permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with Korean licensed banks for hedging USD/KRW import/export trade exposure, limited to genuine commercial transaction amounts and maturities matching the underlying trade cycle

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to non-resident investors or treasury operations that cannot take physical delivery of Korean won, requiring proof of an underlying foreign investment or cross-border obligation and a genuine hedging need

Cross-currency swaps (KRW/USD) permitted for converting foreign currency debt or investment proceeds into Korean won for the Chusik Hoesa's operational use, subject to real-demand confirmation and BOK/FEIN reporting requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convene annual ordinary shareholders meeting and approve annual financial statements, balance sheet, profit and loss statement, and business report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory shareholders meeting; minutes and signed financial statements retained at the registered office; no government filing unless the company is an external-audit target
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court may order convocation upon petition by shareholders holding at least 3% of the shares; directors may be subject to civil damages and an administrative fine up to KRW 5,000,000 (about USD 3,800). Korea does not administratively strike off a company for this event alone, but prolonged governance failure can support creditor petitions for judicial dissolution and, if tax returns are not filed, NTS registration cancellation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top national corporate income tax rate on taxable income above KRW 300 billion; lower brackets 10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion and 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax liability makes the aggregate headline maximum effective rate 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory reductions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for high-tech foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones (100% reduction for five years, 50% for the next two years), R&D expense tax credits up to 25-50% depending on company size, patent/technology transfer income exemption and credit under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, and employment, facility-investment and SME tax incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Corporation Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement / Form 1) filed electronically through HomeTax, the National Tax Service e-filing portal, together with financial statements and supporting schedules relating to taxable income, foreign tax credits and international transactions
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for a December 31 year-end); if a certified tax accountant prepares and signs the return, the filing deadline is extended by 15 days

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Net Income (total revenue less deductible expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Amazon Marketplace gross proceeds, FBA fulfilment fees, freight and advertising grants in Korean won using the Bank of Korea base exchange rate; all worldwide revenue recorded on the books of the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be included irrespective of payout routing through non-resident bank accounts or payment service providers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income after adding non-deductible items and subtracting loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a transfer-pricing adjustment schedule for intercompany payments relating to Amazon FBA fulfilment, marketing, cloud services and warehousing; disallow inflated management fees paid to offshore affiliates lacking functional and economic substance; apply the statutory rules on entertainment expenses, bad debts and capitalisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Corporate Tax on Taxable Income at progressive rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory marginal brackets for the fiscal year; the local income tax surcharge (10% of national corporate tax) is declared separately in the local income tax return and must not be reported in this box; non-resident shareholders use this gross tax line for indirect foreign tax credit computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign Tax Credit for taxes paid in foreign jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the Foreign Tax Credit schedule and attach foreign assessment notices, withholding tax receipts or equivalent supporting documentation; the credit is subject to the per-country limitation computed in Korean won and cannot exceed Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International Tax Adjustments (transfer pricing, thin capitalisation, CFC rules, permanent establishment allocations).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border related-party transactions and provide Local/Master File documentation when applicable; failure to substantiate arm's length pricing can trigger a 10-30% negligent assessment penalty; passive income retained in low-tax jurisdictions may be imputed to Korean shareholders under the Controlled Foreign Corporation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Amount Payable or Refund (gross tax less credits, advance payments and quarterly prepayments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset quarterly prepayments and any Korean-source withholding credits; non-resident payees must file a refund claim within three years of the statutory payment date and provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate if treaty-based refund relief is sought.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, plus a daily accrual of statutory late-payment surcharges until settlement; negligent underreporting is penalised at 10% of the omitted amount, while intentional fraud or unreasonable false returns attract a 40% additional tax; persistent fraud may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, with imprisonment up to 10 years and fines up to three times the tax evaded when the amount concealed exceeds KRW 500 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax under Article 98 of the Corporate Tax Act plus 2% deemed local income tax) on outbound dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder, unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty relief, the non-resident payee must (1) provide a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty jurisdiction, (2) submit to the payer or the competent district tax office an Application for Exemption From or Reduction of Withholding Tax under Tax Treaties before or at the time of payment, (3) prove beneficial ownership of the dividend, interest or royalty, and (4) satisfy any Limitation on Benefits and minimum shareholding/holding period clauses in the relevant treaty; if excess tax was withheld, the recipient may file a refund claim within three years of the statutory payment date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates for outbound interest and royalties are each 22% (20% plus 2% local income tax surcharge); typical treaty rates are 10-15% for royalties and interest, and 5% or 15% for dividends depending on voting power and shareholding percentage, with a TRC, beneficial ownership declaration and absence of a Korean permanent establishment required to access treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; Master File is mandatory when consolidated annual revenue of the Korean group and related parties exceeds KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; Country-by-Country Reports are required for multinational groups meeting statutory global revenue thresholds under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the National Tax Service enforces the substance-over-form principle under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Principal Purpose Test in tax treaties; the Korean Chusik Hoesa must demonstrate real operational substance, local decision-making and Core Income-Generating Activities such as inventory risk, order management, customer contracts and treasury functions in Korea, and a paper entity established solely to obtain tax treaty benefits may be denied treaty access, have its profit re-attributed, or be disregarded for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Amazon FBA sales revenue, creating fictitious logistics and advertising invoices, inflating cost of goods sold with shell suppliers, or concealing sales cash flow in undisclosed foreign bank accounts controlled by the director.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of an unjustified underreporting additional tax equal to 40% of the evaded tax under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; criminal liability under Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, punishable by imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to three times the evaded tax; for amounts over KRW 500 million, the prosecution and collection statute of limitations is extended to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties and surcharges under Articles 38 and 39 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; the National Tax Service can seize personal assets, impose an overseas departure ban, place the director on the high-risk unpaid taxpayer blacklist, and a criminal conviction leads to imprisonment, disqualification from serving as a director, and extradition risk under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Stripping and Shell Entity Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Hong Kong, Nevada, Dubai or other zero-substance shell company to invoice excessive royalties, management fees, marketing service fees or interest from Korea, stripping taxable profits outside Korea while failing to prepare the statutory Local File/Master File or to prove that arm's length remuneration and actual functions, assets and risks reside in the Korean company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recompute Korean taxable income under Articles 4 and 7 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and make a transfer-pricing adjustment, imposing a negligence penalty of 30% of the understated tax amount for missing TP documentation and up to 10% additional penalty for non-arm's length pricing; the foreign payee may also be deemed to have a Korean permanent establishment, triggering branch tax under Article 98-3 of the Corporate Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorised the sham arrangements are jointly and severally liable for the adjusted corporate tax, branch tax and penalties; where the Korean company is found to be the alter ego of the director or shareholders, the tax authority pierces the corporate veil to recover personal assets; criminal tax fraud for abusive profit stripping may result in imprisonment, civil restitution, travel bans and placement on the National Tax Service blacklist.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership / Foreign Exchange Repatriation Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Amazon payouts through layered offshore bank accounts, mixer services or unlicensed payment intermediaries, failing to disclose foreign bank account balances, making disguised dividend distributions through bogus consulting or software fees to foreign shareholders, or repatriating capital without prior tax treaty clearance and foreign-exchange declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, unauthorised or unreported cross-border remittances are punishable by a fine of up to KRW 100 million and imprisonment up to five years; under the Act on Reporting and Using of Certain Financial Transaction Information, failure to report foreign financial accounts or beneficial ownership information attracts a criminal penalty of up to KRW 300 million and imprisonment up to five years, together with asset freezing orders by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director may be ordered to make civil restitution of the repatriated funds and statutory penalties; a criminal conviction triggers confiscation of personally held assets, travel bans, Posting on the financial crime blacklist, disqualification from managing regulated businesses, and imprisonment, while fraudulent concealment may lead to cross-border investigative assistance and asset freezing abroad.
